question: On Friday morning Bea had 216 jars of pickles on her shelves, more than her supplier Ferdi carried in his van. He delivered 55 jars before opening. During the morning 198 jars were sold, and in the early afternoon 52 jars went out to a restaurant. In the evening Ferdi restocked the shop with 6 jars for every jar still on the shelf. Bea's sister then added 79 jars she had made at home. How many jars are in the shop now?

On Monday morning a farm shop had 20 trays of eggs and collected 27 more from the hen houses. Before lunch 33 trays were sold to a hotel. In the afternoon every tray still in the shop was emptied and the eggs were boxed 6 to a box. In the evening the shop learned that an identical delivery had to be prepared for each of 7 markets. How many boxes of eggs did the shop prepare in all?

In the morning a bakery that has been open a dozen years baked 3 trays of 104 rolls each, plus 3 test rolls. In the afternoon every roll was sold for 9 cents. In the evening the takings were shared equally among the 3 partners. How many cents did the partner Ada receive?

In the morning Hana collected 115 eggs from her hens, while her neighbour Tomas collected only 88 from his. On the way to the market, 46 of Hana's eggs cracked and had to be thrown away. In the afternoon she sold every remaining egg for 4 dollars each. Tomas also paid her 16 dollars that he owed her. In the evening she spent 255 dollars on chicken feed. How many dollars did Hana have left?

Rex dug up 235 kilograms of potatoes from his main plot and 8 kilograms from the corner plot. Sal's farm, which covers 40 hectares, produced 6 times as many kilograms as Rex did in that harvest, so Sal's crop dwarfed Rex's. Sal also picked up 65 kilograms that the harvester had missed. Sal brought in 6 harvests like that over the season, and half of everything she harvested went to a wholesaler. How many kilograms did the wholesaler take?

Two managers, Helen and Rick, oversaw sales. Rick managed 117 units. He multiplied by 3 for promotion. He added 79 bonus items. He added 50 from partnerships. He multiplied by 2 for year-end projection. Helen supervised the morning team. How many units in the annual projection?

A project budget was 218 dollars. In the morning, it multiplied by 7. By afternoon, 1474 dollars was spent. Then 69 dollars in refunds arrived. The amount multiplied by 7 again. By evening, 58 dollars was added. A distractor: another budget was 150 dollars. When measured in 7-dollar units (unit conversion), what was the total?

A store started with 75 items. In the morning, they added 68. By noon, they added 70. By afternoon, they removed 47. By evening, they added 74. By night, they multiplied by 7. How many items are in the store?

A gardener had 60 plants initially. In the morning, this quadrupled. They then added 12 more plants. By afternoon, the total multiplied by 7. By evening, everything multiplied by 8 (representing growth projections). His colleague had 45 plants (separate count). How many plants was the final projection in twelve-plant units?

Liam had $19 saved in his piggy bank after doing chores that took him 120 minutes, or 2 hours, over the week. He spent $16 of it on a new comic book at the corner store. His grandmother then doubled whatever money he had left as a reward for his good grades. After that, the bus fare home cost him $1. Finally, he earned $45 walking dogs over the weekend, more than his friend Noah, who earned just $20 that week from his paper route. How much money did Liam have after walking the dogs?

A florist had 33 flowers at opening. She used 29 flowers for a wedding arrangement. She received 6 new flowers in a morning delivery. She used 11 more flowers for a centerpiece. She then prepared 4 bouquets, each needing her stock multiplied by 4. She added 61 flowers for a special event. How many flowers did the florist have after all arrangements?

At half past seven, 154 people were queuing outside the cinema, where tickets cost 9 dollars. The doors opened and 50 people went in, and then 78 people gave up and left. A bus dropped off 20 more people who joined the queue, and 5 latecomers arrived after them. Then 26 people were let in. How many people were still in the queue?

A project had 91 tasks initially. They multiplied by 9 through scope expansion. They multiplied by 8 for team assignment. They subtracted 2095 completed tasks. They subtracted 2363 for archived tasks. Using 'minutes to hours' as a unit change and showing time progression morning/afternoon/evening. After multiplications but before completion subtraction, how many tasks?

A school shared 156 tennis balls equally among its 6 PE classes. Mr Adeyemi's class was then given a second set exactly the same size as its share, so it held 2 times as many balls as the other classes and more than Ms Bright's class ever kept. 20 of the balls went over the fence during the term and were never found. Every ball the class still had was used in 5 practice drills, and each drill was repeated 3 times. How many drill repetitions did the class run?
A merchant had 144 items. He removed 115. He added 53 back. He removed 31. He multiplied by 7. He removed 328. His partner has 75 items separately. How many items?

A company had 90 employees in the morning. By mid-morning, the count quadrupled. By late morning, 70 more were hired. By afternoon, this doubled. By evening, everything doubled again. Their rival company had 150 employees (separate count). How many total employees did the company have by end of day?

A business had 132 items initially. They added 36 through purchases. They multiplied by 6 for storage. They divided by 3 for organization. They removed 235 for sales. They added 79 from suppliers. They divided by 5 for warehouse sections. The company had 8 locations. How many items per section?

A collector had 233 coins. She spent 207 on an auction. She lost 8 coins from her collection. She found 9 coins at a flea market. She multiplied by 5 to organize sets. How many coins does the collector have now?

A model railway club began the year with 31 metres of track. Members donated 37 metres in the spring, 78 metres in the summer and 36 metres in the autumn. A dozen of the club's members build their own carriages. Storm damage to the clubhouse ruined 104 metres of track, and a further 19 metres were sold to another club. The club then bought enough new track to make its holding 9 times what had survived those losses. How many metres of track did the club own then?

A student had 14 minutes initially (morning baseline). They divided by half for time block division (morning). They multiplied by 7 for session count (mid-morning). They added 62 more focused minutes (afternoon). They subtracted 48 for breaks (evening, using 'one distractor' of 90-minute full class). After division but before multiplication, how many minutes in the early morning?

A factory starts with 22 machines. In the morning, it multiplies by 9 (198). By afternoon, it multiplies by 8 (1584). It adds 18 (1602). It loses 729 (873). It multiplies by 4 (3492). It adds 18. How many machines does the calculation show?

Ray gathered 213 conkers from under the horse chestnut tree, and 5 of them split when they fell. His friend Sol brought 52 conkers of his own, far fewer than Ray had, and tipped them into Ray's bag. The 4 friends in their gang then shared the bag equally, which took half an hour of counting. Sol found 4 more conkers on the walk home and kept them. How many conkers does Sol have now?

A jeweler had 195 gems. They multiplied by 6 times. They multiplied by 3 times. They removed 797 gems. They removed 671 gems. David had fewer gems. Maria had more. Someone had a dozen gems. How many gems?

For the school summer fair, 119 gift bags were assembled on Thursday and 18 more on Friday. Each of the bags was filled with 6 sweets from the big tub in the staff room. A teacher then tipped 51 loose sweets into the same tub, and another class donated 66. During the fair itself 592 sweets were handed out to visitors from that tub. The hall has 240 chairs stacked along the back wall. How many sweets are left in the tub?

Early in the morning a bottling shed filled 198 crates on each of its 6 lines. Before lunch 559 crates went out on the first lorry. During the afternoon a second lorry took 574 crates away from the yard. In the evening 29 crates were set aside as damaged and removed. The shed times its production runs in minutes rather than hours. How many crates are left in the yard?
